To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) neighborhood-based graph kernels are a promising approach for computing semantic item similarities; and (2) the proposed CB-RS is a promising approach for recommending items to the user.

a neighborhood-based graph similarity kernel is able to effectively compute the similarity between items and that the use of Linked Data is a great opportunity to improve the quality of the recommendations.

a neighborhood-based graph similarity measure outperforms other competitive similarity measures in a recommender system that leverages linked open data and that the use of linked open data is a promising approach for improving content-based recommender systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a neighborhood-based graph-kernel-based CB-RS for the recommendation of movies.
the development of a neighborhood-based kernel to compute semantic similarities of movie items.

the following research questions: (i) how to leverage the LOD for improving CB-RS accuracy and novelty; (ii) how to exploit a graph kernel for computing item similarities; (iii) how to exploit the neighborhood of the items in order to compute the similarity between them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neighborhood-based graph kernel outperforms the other kernels in the context of the recommender system.
the proposed kernel outperforms the state of the art, and it is a good candidate for a CB-RS.
the proposed approach is able to effectively exploit semantic information from the Web of Data in order to improve the performance of a CB-RS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neighborhood-based graph kernel can be used as a powerful semantic similarity measure for item recommendations.

the neighborhood-based graph kernel is an effective tool that can be used in order to compute item similarities for RSs, especially when the items to be matched have a complex structure and their features are hard to be extracted.
the proposed approach is a good example of the benefits of using Linked Data and neighborhood-based graph kernels to improve RSs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a neighborhood-based graph-kernel is able to capture semantic similarities in a way that can be exploited to improve the quality of a CB-RS.
the use of a neighborhood-based graph kernels in a CB-RS can effectively leverage the LOD to boost the recommendation process.
the proposed neighborhood-based graph kernel is able to effectively compute semantic similarities between items and thus to provide accurate recommendations.
